# Agent Network (2.0) YAML Reference

> For the full documentation index, see: https://docs.mulesoft.com/llms.txt

The `agent-network.yaml` file details the required structure and properties that define your
project’s assets, connections, and policies.

- [Agent Network Section](#agent-network-section)
- [Info Section](#info-section)
- [Registry Section](#registry-section)
- [Context Section](#context-section)
- [Brokers Section](#brokers-section)
- [Expressions Format](#expressions-format)
- [Exchange JSON File](#exchange-json-file)
  - [Runtime System Limits Configuration](#runtime-system-limits)

## Agent Network Section

This is the root section of the agent network. Must include at least one of `registry`, `context`,
or `brokers`.

This section has these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p>info</p></td><td><p>Provides metadata about the graphs.</p></td><td><p><a href="#info-section">info Object</a></p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>agentNetwork</p></td><td><p>This string must be the <a href="#versions">version number</a> of the agent network specification used by the agent network document. This is not related to the document’s <code>info.version</code> property.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>registry</p></td><td><p>Definitions of agents, MCPs, and LLMs.</p></td><td><p><a href="#registry-section">registry</a> Object</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>context</p></td><td><p>Reusable entities scoped to the graphs defined in this file (for example, connections and policies).</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>brokers</p></td><td><p>A mapping of runtime Agent Script definitions that can be executed by the platform.</p></td><td><p><a href="#brokers-section">brokers Object</a></p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

## Info Section

This section contains basic metadata about the agent network document itself.

**Example**

```yaml
info:
  label: Employee Onboarding Workflow
  description: >-
    A multi-agent network for employee onboarding. Orchestrates HR system setup, Salesforce profile
    creation, laptop and badge requests, and Slack notifications for new hires.
  version: 1.0.0
  tags:
    - employee-onboarding
    - multi-agent
    - hr
    - production
```

The section has these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p>label</p></td><td><p>The human-readable name of the agent network.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>version</p></td><td><p>The version number of the <code>agent-network.yaml</code> file.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>description</p></td><td><p>A human readable summary of what the agent network does.  Accepts CommonMark syntax.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>tags</p></td><td><p>Categorization tags for this agent network document.</p></td><td><p>Array of Strings</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>summary</code></p></td><td><p>A short summary of the purpose of the agent network.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>termsOfService</code></p></td><td><p>A URI for the Terms of Service for the API. This must be in the form of a URI.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>contact</code></p></td><td><p>The contact information for the agent network.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>contact.name</code></p></td><td><p>The identifying name of the contact person/organization.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>contact.url</code></p></td><td><p>The URI for the contact information. This must be in the form of a URI.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>contact.email</code></p></td><td><p>The email address of the contact person/organization. This must be in the form of an email address.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>license</code></p></td><td><p>The license information for the agent network.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>license.name</code></p></td><td><p>The license name used for the agent network.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes (if license present)</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>license.identifier</code></p></td><td><p>An SPDX license expression. Mutually exclusive with <code>license.url</code>.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>license.url</code></p></td><td><p>A URI for the license. This must be in the form of a URI. Mutually exclusive with <code>license.identifier</code>.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

## Registry Section

Use this section to organize and reference reusable agents, LLMs, and MCP tools. The registry
section defined in the file is considered the "local registry". Assets defined in the registry are
published to Exchange.

**Example**

```yaml
registry:
  agents:
    hr-system-agent:
      info:
        label: HR System Agent
        description: Agent that creates new-hire records and manages HR system setup.
      metadata:
        platform: AgentForce
        interfaces:
          a2a:
            card:
              name: hr-system-agent
              description: Creates and manages employee records in the HR system.
              url: https://hr-agent.example.com/a2a
              version: "1.0.0"
              protocolVersion: "1.0"
              capabilities: {}
              defaultInputModes: [application/json, text/plain]
              defaultOutputModes: [application/json, text/plain]
              skills: []
        tools:
          - mcp:
              ref:
                name: slack-mcp
              allowed: [sendMessage, listChannels]
        llm:
          ref:
            name: Open-AI-LLM
    salesforce-agent:
      info:
        label: Salesforce Onboarding Agent
        description: Agent that provisions Salesforce profiles for new hires.
      metadata:
        platform: AgentForce
        interfaces:
          a2a:
            card:
              name: salesforce-agent
              description: Onboards new employees to Salesforce.
              url: https://sfdc-agent.example.com/a2a
              version: "1.0.0"
              protocolVersion: "1.0"
              capabilities: {}
              defaultInputModes: [application/json]
              defaultOutputModes: [application/json]
              skills: []
        llm:
          ref:
            name: Open-AI-LLM
  mcps:
    slack-mcp:
      info:
        label: Slack MCP Server
        description: MCP server for sending messages and listing Slack channels.
      metadata:
        protocolVersion: "2024-11-05"
        transport:
          kind: sse
          ssePath: /mcp
        tools:
          - name: sendMessage
            description: Send a message to a Slack channel.
            inputSchema:
              type: object
              properties:
                text: { type: string }
                channelId: { type: string }
          - name: listChannels
            description: List available Slack channels.
            inputSchema:
              type: object
  llms:
    Open-AI-LLM:
      info:
        label: OpenAI LLM
        description: OpenAI provider for orchestration and generation nodes.
      metadata:
        platform: OpenAI
        models:
          - gpt-4o
          - gpt-4o-mini
          - gpt5-mini
    Azure-OpenAI-LLM:
      info:
        label: Azure OpenAI LLM
        description: Azure OpenAI for orchestration nodes.
      metadata:
        platform: AzureOpenai
        models:
          - gpt-4o
```

The `registry` section has these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th><th>Values</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p><code>agents</code></p></td><td><p>The list of agents defined as part of this network.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p>Keys: identifiers matching ^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]*$. Values: AgentEntity</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>mcps</code></p></td><td><p>The list of MCP servers defined as part of this network.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p>Keys: identifiers. Values: MCPServerEntity</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>llms</code></p></td><td><p>The list of LLM providers defined as part of this network.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p>Keys: identifiers. Values: LLMEntityEach <code>LLMEntity</code> requires <code>metadata.platform</code>: <code>Gemini</code>, <code>OpenAI</code>, or <code>AzureOpenai</code>.</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

### Info

All nodes in this section share these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p><code>label</code></p></td><td><p>The human readable short text.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>description</code></p></td><td><p>A human readable text of what this element does. Accepts CommonMark syntax.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>tags</code></p></td><td><p>Optional tags.</p></td><td><p>Array of Strings</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

### Agents

Each registry agent is an `AgentEntity`. The schema requires a `metadata` object. The interfaces,
tools, and LLM reference are nested under `metadata`, not at the root of the agent.

The agents section has these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p><code>agents.info</code></p></td><td><p>Metadata for the agent.</p></td><td><p>InfoObject</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>agents.metadata</code></p></td><td><p>Platform, interfaces, tools, and LLM wiring for the agent.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>agents.metadata.platform</code></p></td><td><p>Host platform for the agent (for example, AgentForce or Bedrock).</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>agents.metadata.interfaces</code></p></td><td><p>The interfaces that this agent supports. At least one of <code>a2a</code>, <code>a2a_v03</code>, or <code>other</code> must be present.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>agents.metadata.interfaces.a2a</code></p></td><td><p>A2A protocol version 1.x interface definition. Contains the agent card.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>No (at least one interface required)</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>agents.metadata.interfaces.a2a.card</code></p></td><td><p>The A2A v1 agent card. See <a href="#a2a-card">A2A Card</a>.</p></td><td><p>AgentCard</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>agents.metadata.interfaces.a2a_v03</code></p></td><td><p>A2A protocol version 0.3.x interface definition (legacy).</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>No (at least one interface required)</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>agents.metadata.interfaces.a2a_v03.card</code></p></td><td><p>The A2A v0.3 agent card.</p></td><td><p>AgentCard</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>agents.metadata.interfaces.other</code></p></td><td><p>Other protocol interface definition.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>No (at least one interface required)</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>agents.metadata.interfaces.other.protocol</code></p></td><td><p>The protocol name for this interface.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes (when using other)</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>agents.metadata.interfaces.other.card</code></p></td><td><p>The card for this protocol.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>agents.urls</code></p></td><td><p>Named URLs for the agent.</p></td><td><p>Array</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>agents.metadata.tools</code></p></td><td><p>The list of tool providers (MCP or A2A)</p></td><td><p>Array[Object]</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>agents.metadata.llm</code></p></td><td><p>Reference to the LLM used by this agent (ref to a declared LLM)</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

Authentication for outbound calls is configured on [`connections`](#connections) (and related
policies), not on registry `AgentEntity` definitions.

> [!NOTE] If you are connecting to an agent that uses A2A protocol version 0.3.x, use the `a2a_v03`
> interface key instead of `a2a`. The `a2a` key targets A2A protocol version 1.x.

#### A2A Card

This section adheres to the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) specification v1.0 and describes an agent’s
contract, skills, and capabilities. This is a standard A2A agent card
[as defined in the Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol specification](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/#441-agentcard).

The A2A card section has these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th><th>Values</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p><code>name</code></p></td><td><p>Human-readable name for the agent.</p></td><td><p>string</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td><td><p> — </p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>description</code></p></td><td><p>Human-readable description of the agent’s purpose.</p></td><td><p>string</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td><td><p> — </p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>url</code></p></td><td><p>Preferred endpoint URL for interacting with the agent. Must support preferredTransport.</p></td><td><p>string</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td><td><p>for example, <a href="https://api.example.com/a2a/v1">https://api.example.com/a2a/v1</a></p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>version</code></p></td><td><p>Agent’s own version number (format defined by provider).</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td><td><p>for example, 1.0.0</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>protocolVersion</code></p></td><td><p>Version of the A2A protocol this agent supports.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td><td><p>for example, 1.0</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>capabilities</code></p></td><td><p>Optional capabilities supported by the agent.</p></td><td><p>AgentCapabilities</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td><td><p>See below</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>defaultInputModes</code></p></td><td><p>Default supported input MIME types for all skills (overridable per skill).</p></td><td><p>Array of string</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td><td><p> — </p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>defaultOutputModes</code></p></td><td><p>Default supported output MIME types for all skills (overridable per skill).</p></td><td><p>Array of string</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td><td><p> — </p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>skills</code></p></td><td><p>The set of skills or distinct capabilities the agent can perform.</p></td><td><p>Array of AgentSkills</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td><td><p>See below</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>preferredTransport</code></p></td><td><p>Transport for the main url. Must be available at that URL.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p>JSON-RPC, GRPC, HTTP JSON (default: JSON-RPC)</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>additionalInterfaces</code></p></td><td><p>Additional transport+URL combinations for the same agent.</p></td><td><p>Array of AgentInterface</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p>Each: { transport: string, url: string }</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>additionalInterfaces.transport</code></p></td><td><p>The transport protocol for this interface.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td><td><p><code>JSONRPC, GRPC, HTTP+JSON)</code></p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>additionalInterfaces.url</code></p></td><td><p>The URL for this additional interface.</p></td><td><p>String (URI)</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td><td><p>Valid URI string</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>provider</code></p></td><td><p>Agent’s service provider.</p></td><td><p>AgentProvider</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p>{ organization: string, url: string }</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>documentationUrl</code></p></td><td><p>Optional URL to the agent’s documentation.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p> — </p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>iconUrl</code></p></td><td><p>Optional URL to an icon for the agent.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p> — </p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>security</code></p></td><td><p>Security requirement objects for all interactions (OpenAPI 3.0 style; OR of ANDs).</p></td><td><p>Array of object</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p>Each object: scheme names → array of scope strings</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>securitySchemes</code></p></td><td><p>Declared security schemes (key \= scheme name). OpenAPI 3.0 Security Scheme Object.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p>apiKey, http, oauth2, openIdConnect, mutualTLS</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>signatures</code></p></td><td><p>JSON Web Signatures for this AgentCard (RFC 7515 JWS).</p></td><td><p>Array of AgentCardSignature</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p>{ protected, signature, header? }</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

##### Skills Properties

Skills describe the distinct capabilities the agent can perform and have these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Valid Values</th><th>Required</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p><code>id</code></p></td><td><p>Unique identifier for the skill.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Any string value</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>name</code></p></td><td><p>A human-readable name for the skill.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Any string value</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>description</code></p></td><td><p>A description of what this skill does.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Any string value</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>examples</code></p></td><td><p>Usage examples demonstrating how to use this skill.</p></td><td><p>Array of strings</p></td><td><p>Array of example strings</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>inputModes</code></p></td><td><p>Supported input MIME types for this skill (overrides defaultInputModes).</p></td><td><p>Array of strings</p></td><td><p>Array of MIME type strings</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>outputModes</code></p></td><td><p>Supported output MIME types for this skill (overrides defaultOutputModes).</p></td><td><p>Array of strings</p></td><td><p>Array of MIME type strings</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>tags</code></p></td><td><p>Categorization tags for this skill.</p></td><td><p>Array of strings</p></td><td><p>Array of tag strings</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

##### Capabilities Properties

Capabilities describe optional features supported by the agent and have these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Valid Values</th><th>Required</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p><code>streaming</code></p></td><td><p>Indicates if the agent supports streaming responses.</p></td><td><p>Boolean</p></td><td><p><code>true</code> or <code>false</code></p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>pushNotifications</code></p></td><td><p>Indicates if the agent supports push notifications.</p></td><td><p>Boolean</p></td><td><p><code>true</code> or <code>false</code></p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>extendedAgentCard</code></p></td><td><p>Indicates if the agent supports providing an extended agent card when authenticated.</p></td><td><p>Boolean</p></td><td><p><code>true</code> or <code>false</code></p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>extensions</code></p></td><td><p>List of protocol extensions supported by the agent.</p></td><td><p>Array</p></td><td><p>Array of extension objects</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

### MCP

The MCP Server section has these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th><th>Values</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p><code>info</code></p></td><td><p>Metadata for the MCP Server</p></td><td><p><code>InfoObject</code></p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p> — </p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>urls</code></p></td><td><p>Named URLs for the MCP server.</p></td><td><p>Array</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p> — </p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>metadata</code></p></td><td><p>MCP server descriptor (how to connect and what it exposes).</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td><td><p> — </p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>metadata.protocolVersion</code></p></td><td><p>Version of the MCP protocol.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p>"2024-11-05", "2025-03-26", "2025-06-18", "2025-11-25"</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>metadata.transport</code></p></td><td><p>Transport experimental, tasks, logging, prompts, resources, tools</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>metadata.tools</code></p></td><td><p>List of tools.</p></td><td><p>Array</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p>action definitions</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>metadata.resources</code></p></td><td><p>List of resources.</p></td><td><p>Array</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p>Resource definitions</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>metadata.resourceTemplates</code></p></td><td><p>List of resource templates.</p></td><td><p>Array</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p>ResourceTemplate definitions</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>metadata.prompts</code></p></td><td><p>List of prompts.</p></td><td><p>Array</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p>Prompt definitions</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>metadata.platform</code></p></td><td><p>Platform the MCP server runs on.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p> — </p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>metadata.securitySchemes</code></p></td><td><p>Security schemes for authentication.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p>SecurityScheme by key</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

#### MCP Transport types

The `metadata.transport` object describes how clients connect to the MCP server. The supported
transport kinds are `sse`, `streamableHttp`, and `stdio`.

**Example**

```yaml
registry:
  mcps:
    weather-mcp:
      metadata:
        protocolVersion: "2025-06-18"
        transport:
          kind: streamableHttp
          path: /weather/mcp
        provider:
          organization: Acme Inc.
          url: https://www.acme.com
    my-mcp-sse:
      metadata:
        transport:
          kind: sse
          ssePath: /mcp/sse
          messagesPath: /mcp
```

##### SseTransport

Sse Transport has these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th><th>Values</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p><code>kind</code></p></td><td><p>Transport type.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td><td><p><code>"sse"</code></p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>ssePath</code></p></td><td><p>Path to the SSE endpoint.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td><td><p> — </p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>messagesPath</code></p></td><td><p>Path to the messages endpoint.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p>Agent Graph Expression Optional</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

##### StreamableHttpTransport

StreamableHttpTransport has these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th><th>Values</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p><code>kind</code></p></td><td><p>Transport type.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td><td><p>"streamableHttp"</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>path</code></p></td><td><p>Path to the MCP endpoint.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p> — </p></td></tr></tbody></table>

StdioTransport has these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th><th>Values</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p><code>kind</code></p></td><td><p>Transport type.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td><td><p><code>"stdio"</code></p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>instructions</code></p></td><td><p>Instructions to run the MCP server.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p> — </p></td></tr></tbody></table>

### Reference Types

Reference types are reusable objects that point to other entities defined in the registry, such as
agents, MCP servers, LLMs, connections, and policies.

**Example**

```yaml
registry:
  agents:
    myEvaluationAgent:
      type: a2a_agent
      protocol: a2a
      platform: agentforce
      kind: evaluation
      connections:
        - kind: mcp
          ref:
            assetId: my-mcp-server
            version: 1.0.0
          allowed:
            - tool-name-1
      provenance:
        kind: exchange
        metadata:
          organizationId: my-org
```

Reference types used in the Registry section have these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Reference</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th><th>Values</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p><code>AgentRef</code></p></td><td><p>Reference to an agent.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p><code>{ name: string, namespace?: string }</code></p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>MCPRef</code></p></td><td><p>Reference to an MCP server.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p><code>{ name: string, namespace?: string }</code></p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>LLMRef</code></p></td><td><p>Reference to an LLM provider.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p><code>{ name: string, namespace?: string }</code></p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>ConnectionRef</code></p></td><td><p>Reference to a connection.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p><code>{ name: string }</code></p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>PolicyRef</code></p></td><td><p>Reference to a policy.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p><code>{ name: string, namespace?: string }</code></p></td></tr></tbody></table>

## Context Section

This section is for reusable entities scoped to the graphs defined in the `agent-network.yaml` file.
It holds definitions that are used by the document (for example, connections, policies) but are not
published to the agent registry.

**Example**

```yaml
context:
  connections:
    hr_system_agent:
      kind: a2a
      ref:
        name: hr-system-agent
      url: https://hr-agent.example.com/a2a
      policies:
        outbound:
          - ref:
              name: retry-policy
    salesforce_agent:
      kind: a2a
      ref:
        name: salesforce-agent
      url: https://sfdc-agent.example.com/a2a
    slack_mcp:
      kind: mcp
      ref:
        name: slack-mcp
      url: https://mcp.example.com/slack
    openai_llm:
      kind: llm
      ref:
        name: Open-AI-LLM
      url: https://api.openai.com/v1
      authentication:
        kind: apiKey
  policies:
    retry-policy:
      ref:
        name: retry-policy
      configuration:
        maxAttempts: 3
        backoffMs: 1000
```

The `context` section has these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p>connections</p></td><td><p>The list of connections defined as part of this network.</p></td><td><p>Connection Objects</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>policies</p></td><td><p>Policy definitions that govern connection behavior, access, and execution.</p></td><td><p>Policies Object</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

### Connections

Connection definitions live in the `context` object. Each `connections` object has a kind field that
determines its connection type: either `a2a`, `llm`, or `mcp`.

#### Connection ID Format

Each connection key (ID) must use only:

- Lowercase letters (`a`–`z`)
- Numeric characters (`0`–`9`)
- Underscores (`_`), non-trailing

For example, `hr_system_agent` and `slack_mcp` are valid, but `HR-System-Agent` and `my_connection_`
are not.

Connection objects have these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Field Name</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p><code>kind</code></p></td><td><p>Connection type</p></td><td><p><code>mcp</code>, <code>a2a</code>, or <code>llm</code></p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>ref</code></p></td><td><p>A reference to an asset representing the target system.</p></td><td><p>Reference Object</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>url</code></p></td><td><p>The base URL of the target system.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>authentication</code></p></td><td><p>The authentication method to use when connecting to the target system.</p></td><td><p>Authentication Object</p></td><td><p>No (Yes for <code>llm</code> connections)</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>policies</code></p></td><td><p>Policy bindings to apply to this connection, organized by traffic direction.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>policies.inbound</code></p></td><td><p>Policy bindings applied to inbound traffic.</p></td><td><p>Array</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>policies.outbound</code></p></td><td><p>Policy bindings applied to outbound traffic.</p></td><td><p>Array</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

You can attach policies to connection objects by referencing their policy identifier or by defining
an inline policy binding. See the [policies object](#policies) for field definitions.

### Policies

This section describes reusable, composable policy bindings and definitions that govern specific
behaviors or constraints related to connections. You must reference the policy identifier to attach
a policy.

For more information about applying policies via Flex Gateway in Local Mode, see:

- [Securing Agent Interactions with Flex Gateway](https://docs.mulesoft.com/gateway/latest/flex-agent-secure)
- [Applying Policies in Local Mode](https://docs.mulesoft.com/gateway/latest/flex-gateway-secure-local)

**Example**

```yaml
context:
  policies:
    myRateLimitPolicy:
      ref:
        name: myReferenceObject
      configuration:
        - rate: 100
          unit: minute
```

This section has these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p>ref</p></td><td><p>Reference to a specific policy definition.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>ref.name</p></td><td><p>Name of the reference definition</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>configuration</p></td><td><p>Policy-specific configuration (structure defined by the referenced policy definition).</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

### Authentication

This section defines the authentication schemes used by the agent network for authenticating when
making outbound requests.

#### Basic Client Authentication

HTTP Basic authentication with username and password.

**Example**

```yaml
kind: basic username: my-username password: my-password headerName: Authorization
```

The basic object has these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Valid Values</th><th>Required</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p>kind</p></td><td><p>The authentication method type.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>basic</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>username</p></td><td><p>Username for authentication.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>password</p></td><td><p>Password for authentication.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>headerName</p></td><td><p>The name of the HTTP used for basic credentials. If not specified, Authorization is used.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>String. Defaults to Authorization.</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

#### API Key Client Authentication

Authenticates outbound requests by including an API key in a configurable HTTP header.

**Example**

```yaml
kind: apiKey apiKey: my-api-key-123 headerName: Authorization
```

An API key passed in a header has these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Valid Values</th><th>Required</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p>kind</p></td><td><p>The authentication method type.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>apiKey</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>headerName</p></td><td><p>The name of the HTTP header that carries the API key. If not specified, Authorization is used.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>String. Defaults to Authorization.</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>apiKey</p></td><td><p>The header or parameter name for the API key.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

#### API Key Client Credentials Client Authentication

API key client credentials with client ID and client secret objects.

**Example**

```yaml
type: apikey-client-credentials client-id:
   value: my-client-id
   name: client_id client-secret:
   value: my-client-secret
   name: client_secret
```

The API key client credentials object has these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Valid Values</th><th>Required</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p>kind</p></td><td><p>The authentication method type.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>apikey-client-credentials</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>clientId</p></td><td><p>Description of the client ID to be used.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>Object with value and optional name (default header name is client_id).</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>clientId.value</p></td><td><p>The value for the client ID.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>clientId.name</p></td><td><p>The header or parameter name.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>clientSecret</p></td><td><p>Description of the client secret to be used.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>Object with value and optional name (default header name is client_secret).</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>clientSecret.value</p></td><td><p>The value for the client secret.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>clientSecret.name</p></td><td><p>The header or parameter name.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

#### OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials Grant Client Authentication

OAuth 2.0 authentication using the Client Credentials Grant Type. Allows agents to obtain access
tokens using a client ID and client secret from the token provider.

**Example**

```yaml
kind: oauth2-client-credentials clientId: my-client-id clientSecret: my-client-secret token:
   url: https://my-oauth2-provider.com/token
   timeout: 15
   bodyEncoding: form scopes:
   - my.custom.scope
   - another.scope
```

The oauth2-client-credentials object has these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Valid Values</th><th>Required</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p>kind</p></td><td><p>The authentication method type.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>oauth2-client-credentials</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>clientId</p></td><td><p>The client ID to authenticate with the OAuth2 provider.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>clientSecret</p></td><td><p>The client secret used with client ID.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>token</p></td><td><p>Configuration for how to fetch the token.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>Token object</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>token.url</p></td><td><p>The URL of the token provider (token endpoint).</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Valid URL string</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>token.timeout</p></td><td><p>Time in seconds to wait for the token service to respond.</p></td><td><p>Number</p></td><td><p>Any number</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>token.bodyEncoding</p></td><td><p>Content encoding for the request body. (<code>form = application/x-www-form-urlencoded</code>, <code>json = application/json</code>)</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p><code>form</code> or <code>json</code></p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>scopes</p></td><td><p>Array of scopes to request during token retrieval.</p></td><td><p>Array</p></td><td><p>Array of scope strings. Defaults to []</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

#### In-Task Authorization Code

Use in-task authorization code when the connection needs secondary credentials obtained during a
task using the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow. OAuth2 tokens are extracted from message data and
injected into the Authorization header for upstream calls. This supports step-up or in-task
authentication (for example, when a user must re-authenticate for a sensitive action). For more
information about the associated policy, see
[A2A In-Task Authorization Code Policy](../../gateway/latest/policies-outbound-a2a-intask-authorization-code).

**Example**

```yaml
authentication:
   kind: in-task-authorization-code
   secondaryAuthProvider: providerName
   authorizationEndpoint: https://oauth.provider.com/authorize
   tokenEndpoint: https://oauth.provider.com/token
   scopes: Read
   redirectUri: https://oauth.provider.com/callback
   responseType: code
   tokenAudience: https://api.example.com/agents/my-agent
   codeChallengeMethod: S256
   bodyEncoding: form
   challengeResponseStatusCode: 200
    tokenTimeout: 300
```

The in-task-authorization-code authentication has these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Valid Values</th><th>Required</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p>kind</p></td><td><p>Authentication type.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>in-task-authorization-code</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>authorizationEndpoint</p></td><td><p>OAuth2 authorization endpoint URL. Used to generate the authentication challenge.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Valid URL</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>tokenEndpoint</p></td><td><p>OAuth2 token endpoint URL. Used to generate the authentication challenge.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Valid URL</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>scopes</p></td><td><p>OAuth2 scopes required for step-up authentication.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Space- or comma-separated scope list (for example, openid profile email)</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>redirectUri</p></td><td><p>OAuth2 redirect URI the client uses in the authorization flow.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Valid URI</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>secondaryAuthProvider</p></td><td><p>Name of the IdP (for example, okta, auth0). Informational only, for the authentication card.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Any string</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>responseType</p></td><td><p>OAuth2 response type.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Typically code. Default: code</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>codeChallengeMethod</p></td><td><p>PKCE code challenge method.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Typically S256. Default: S256</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>tokenAudience</p></td><td><p>Intended recipient of the token (for example, agent1 or API URL).</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Any string</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>bodyEncoding</p></td><td><p>Encoding for the token request body.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>form, json. Default: form</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>tokenTimeout</p></td><td><p>Timeout in seconds for token requests.</p></td><td><p>Integer</p></td><td><p>Positive integer. Default: 300</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>challengeResponseStatusCode</p></td><td><p>HTTP status code returned for auth-required challenge responses. Typically 200 for JSON-RPC compatibility.</p></td><td><p>Integer</p></td><td><p>HTTP status code. Default: 200</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>distributed</p></td><td><p>Share token cache across replicas. Required for fully managed gateway or any multi-replica deployment.</p></td><td><p>Boolean</p></td><td><p><code>true</code> or <code>false</code>. Default: <code>false</code></p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>subjectTokenType</p></td><td><p>The token type identifier for the subject token.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Default: <code>urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token</code></p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>requestedTokenType</p></td><td><p>The desired token type for the issued token.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Any string</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

#### OAuth 2.0 OBO Credential Injection

This authentication type supports OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange and Microsoft Entra ID On-Behalf-Of
protocols. For more information about the associated policy, see
[OAuth 2.0 OBO Credential Injection Policy](../../gateway/latest/policies-outbound-oauth-obo).

**Using OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange**

```yaml
authentication:
  kind: oauth2-obo
  flow: oauth2-token-exchange
  tokenEndpoint: https://oauth.provider.com/token
  targetType: audience
  targetValue: https://api.example.com/agents/my-agent
  scope: Read #optional, OAuth 2.0 scope to request. Required for Microsoft Entra OBO (for example, api://downstream-client-id/.default). Optional for OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693).
  timeout: 5000
```

**Using Microsoft Entra ID On-Behalf-Of**

```yaml
authentication:
  kind: oauth2-obo
  flow: microsoft-entra-obo
  tokenEndpoint: https://oauth.provider.com/token
  scope: api://downstream-client-id/.default
  timeout: 5000
```

The `oauth2-obo` authentication has these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Valid Values</th><th>Required</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p>kind</p></td><td><p>Authentication type.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>oauth2-obo</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>flow</p></td><td><p>Token exchange flow type.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>oauth2-token-exchange, microsoft-entra-obo</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>clientId</p></td><td><p>OAuth2 client ID for token exchange.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>clientSecret</p></td><td><p>OAuth2 client secret for token exchange.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>tokenEndpoint</p></td><td><p>OAuth2 token endpoint URL for token exchange.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Valid URL</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>targetType</p></td><td><p>Parameter type for specifying the target service (audience for logical name, resource for physical URI). Used for OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>audience, resource. Default: audience</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>targetValue</p></td><td><p>Target audience URI or resource URI for the exchanged token. Required for OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Valid URI</p></td><td><p>Required when using oauth2-token-exchange with a target</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>scope</p></td><td><p>OAuth scope to request. Required for Microsoft Entra OBO (for example, api://downstream-client-id/.default). Optional for OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Required for microsoft-entra-obo</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>timeout</p></td><td><p>Timeout for token exchange requests in milliseconds.</p></td><td><p>Integer</p></td><td><p>Positive integer. Default: 10000</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>cibaEnabled</p></td><td><p>When <code>true</code>, it uses Client Initiated Backchannel Authentication (CIBA) instead of standard OBO token exchange. Only valid when <code>flow</code> is <code>oauth2-token-exchange</code>.</p></td><td><p>Boolean</p></td><td><p><code>true</code> or <code>false</code>. Default: <code>false</code></p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>cibaEndpoint</p></td><td><p>Backchannel authorization (<code>bc-authorize</code>) endpoint URL for CIBA.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Valid URL</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>cibaLoginHintClaim</p></td><td><p>JWT claim from the subject token to send as the CIBA <code>login_hint</code> (for example, <code>email,</code> <code>sub</code>).</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>String. Default: <code>email</code></p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>cibaBindingMessage</p></td><td><p>Optional message shown on the user’s authentication device during CIBA approval.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>distributed</p></td><td><p>Share token cache across replicas. Required for fully managed gateway or any multi-replica deployment.</p></td><td><p>Boolean</p></td><td><p><code>true</code> or <code>false</code>. Default: <code>false</code></p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

## Brokers Section

Use this section to define brokers that orchestrate and control the flow of agent and tool
invocations. Each broker object maps to an `.agent` file. You can have multiple Agent Script files
in your `/brokers` directory.

### Broker ID Format

Each broker key (ID) must use only:

- Lowercase letters (`a`–`z`)
- Numeric characters (`0`–`9`)
- Underscores (`_`), non-trailing

For example, `customer_service_agent` and `billing_agent` are valid, but `customerServiceAgent` and
`my_broker_` are not.

**Example**

```yaml
brokers:
  customer_service_agent:
    kind: AgentScript
    implementation: ./brokers/customer-service.agent
    interfaces:
      a2a:
        card: ...
        policies:
          inbound:
            - ref:
                name: rate-limit-policy
  billing_agent:
    kind: AgentScript
    implementation: ./brokers/billing-handler.agent
    interfaces:
      a2a:
        card: ...
```

The `brokers` section has these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th><th>Values</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p><code><em>(broker id)</em></code></p></td><td><p>Named broker definition. See <a href="#broker-id-format">Broker ID Format</a>.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>No</p></td><td><p>Keys: identifiers using only lowercase <code>a</code>–<code>z</code>, <code>0</code>–<code>9</code>, and non-trailing underscores (<code>_</code>). Values: broker entity (BrokerEntity in agent_network_v2.json)</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>kind</code></p></td><td><p>The type of agent implementation.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td><td><p><code>AgentScript</code></p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>implementation</code></p></td><td><p>The path to the Agent Script implementation file.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td><td><p> — </p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>interfaces</code></p></td><td><p>Exposed interfaces for this broker.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td><td><p><code>a2a</code></p></td></tr></tbody></table>

### interfaces.a2a

The `a2a` interface defines how external clients interact with a broker through the Agent2Agent
protocol. It contains the broker’s agent card and any inbound or outbound policy bindings.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p><code>card</code></p></td><td><p>The A2A agent card. See <a href="#a2a-card">A2A Card</a>.</p></td><td><p>AgentCard</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>policies</code></p></td><td><p>Inbound and outbound policy binding lists for this interface.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>policies.inbound</code></p></td><td><p>Policy bindings for inbound traffic.</p></td><td><p>Array</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>policies.outbound</code></p></td><td><p>Policy bindings for outbound traffic.</p></td><td><p>Array</p></td><td><p>No</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

#### User Identity and Task Security

The broker derives a `userId` from the authentication context of the security policy applied at the
broker’s ingress. This `userId` secures
[A2A task management operations](af-agent-script-reference#a2a-trigger), ensuring that only the
authenticated user who owns a task can query or modify it. This includes `SendMessage` and
`SendStreamingMessage` operations that target an existing task.

If no authentication policy is configured at the broker’s ingress, or if a `userId` cannot be
determined from the authentication context, the broker continues to orchestrate normally. However,
A2A task management operations (such as querying task status, canceling a task, or sending messages
to an existing task) are not available for tasks created without an associated `userId`.

#### Policy Binding Reference

Use a policy binding reference to attach a previously declared policy to a broker interface by name.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p><code>ref.name</code></p></td><td><p>Name of the declared policy binding. See <a href="#policies">Policies</a>.</p></td><td><p>String</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

#### Inline Policy Binding

Use an inline policy binding to define a policy directly on the broker interface without declaring
it elsewhere first.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Parameter</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p><code>policy</code></p></td><td><p>The policy to be applied.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>policy.ref</code></p></td><td><p>Reference to the policy definition.</p></td><td><p>PolicyRef See <a href="#policies">Policies</a>.</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p><code>policy.configuration</code></p></td><td><p>Policy-specific configuration.</p></td><td><p>Object</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

## Expressions Format

Use Python expressions to resolve or calculate values that are only available at runtime.

Enclose expressions using the {{}} evaluation wrapper. You can also use multiline statements using
the [appropriate YAML syntax](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/#54-line-break-characters).

**Example**

```yaml
- reasoning:
    id: welcome-message
    description: "Send a welcome message to the candidate."
    llm: my-primary-llm
    prompt:
      "Extract the email from {{input}} and send a greeting email to the user saying their
      onboarding process has started"
    tools:
      - ref: my-email-tool
```

Expressions have these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Variable Name</th><th>Description</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p>input</p></td><td><p>Payload or parameters provided as input to the node.</p></td><td><p>Type defined by Graph</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>variables</p></td><td><p>A mutable key-value store for variables scoped to the execution of the graph instance.</p></td><td><p>Dict[string, any]</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>{node-ids}</p></td><td><p>Read-only mapping of all node definitions available in the current graph, indexed by node id.</p></td><td><p>Dict[string, Object]</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

{node-ids} have these properties.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Variable Name</th><th>Type</th><th>Description</th><th>Required</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p>input</p></td><td><p>Type defined by Graph</p></td><td><p>Input to the node as it happened.</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>output</p></td><td><p>Type defined by Graph</p></td><td><p>Output provided by the node as it happened</p></td><td><p>Yes</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

## Exchange.JSON File

All agent network projects have an `exchange.json` file. This file contains asset metadata available
in Anypoint Exchange after publishing your agent network assets.

**Example**

```json
{
  "main": "agent-network.yaml",
  "name": "Employee Onboarding Network",
  "classifier": "agentic-network",
  "organizationId": "85de5a54-1f33-4ea4-a1bf-8a65bc409179",
  "descriptorVersion": "1.0.0",
  "tags": [],
  "groupId": "85de5a54-1f33-4ea4-a1bf-8a65bc409179",
  "assetId": "employee-onboarding-network",
  "version": "1.0.5",
  "dependencies": [
    {
      "groupId": "85de5a54-1f33-4ea4-a1bf-8a65bc409179",
      "assetId": "hr-agent",
      "version": "1.0.21",
      "classifier": "agent-metadata",
      "packaging": "zip"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "variables": {
      "openai": {
        "clientId": {
          "description": "OpenAI LLM Client ID",
          "default": ""
        },
        "clientSecret": {
          "description": "OpenAI LLM Client Secret",
          "default": "",
          "secret": true
        },
        "url": {
          "description": "OpenAI URL",
          "default": "",
          "secret": false
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

These key-value pairs are important for your agent network configuration:

- groupId: ID of the Anypoint business group that owns your agent network and all the assets derived
  from it.
- assetId: Unique identifier for the agent network project.
- dependencies: Existing assets that this network needs to reference.
- variables: Nested in the metadata section, defines all the variables whose values shouldn’t be
  hardcoded in the `agent-network.yaml` file. Enter these values when publishing the agent network.
  Each variable has a description value, a default value, and a secret value that indicates whether
  it’s treated as sensitive or not.

### Runtime System Limits Configuration

You can configure runtime system limits for your agent network by adding specific variables to the
`metadata.variables` section of your `exchange.json` file. These variables control graph execution
behavior and help prevent infinite loops or excessive resource usage.

**Example**

```json
{
  "main": "agent-network.yaml",
  "name": "it-investigation-GA-version",
  "classifier": "agentic-network",
  "organizationId": "{YOUR ORG ID}",
  "descriptorVersion": "1.0.0",
  "tags": [],
  "metadata": {
    "variables": {
      "openai": {
        "apiKey": {
          "description": "OpenAI API key",
          "default": "",
          "secret": true
        }
      },
      "MODULE_GRAPH_ERROR_SETTINGS_MAX_HANDOFF_ITERATIONS": {
        "description": "max node-to-node transitions per turn",
        "secret": false,
        "default": "30"
      },
      "MODULE_GRAPH_ERROR_SETTINGS_MAX_REASONING_ITERATIONS": {
        "description": "max LLM reasoning loops within a single node",
        "secret": false,
        "default": "20"
      },
      "MODULE_GRAPH_ERROR_SETTINGS_MAX_SUBGRAPH_DEPTH": {
        "description": "max subgraph nesting depth",
        "secret": false,
        "default": "10"
      },
      "MODULE_GRAPH_ERROR_SETTINGS_MAX_NODE_TOOL_CALL_ITERATIONS": {
        "description": "max tool_executor runs per node",
        "secret": false,
        "default": "20"
      },
      "MODULE_GRAPH_ERROR_SETTINGS_MAX_TURN_TOOL_CALL_COUNTS": {
        "description": "total tool invocations across all nodes per turn",
        "secret": false,
        "default": "50"
      },
      "MODULE_GRAPH_ERROR_SETTINGS_MAX_STATE_SIZE_BYTES": {
        "description": "max accumulated state size in bytes (10 MB)",
        "secret": false,
        "default": "10485760"
      }
    }
  },
  "apiVersion": "v1.0",
  "dependencies": [],
  "groupId": "{YOUR ORG ID}",
  "assetId": "it-investigation-GA-version",
  "version": "1.0.0"
}
```

#### Runtime System Limit Variables

The following table describes the runtime system limit variables you can configure:

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Variable Name</th><th>Description</th><th>Default Value</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p>MODULE_GRAPH_ERROR_SETTINGS_MAX_HANDOFF_ITERATIONS</p></td><td><p>Maximum number of node-to-node transitions allowed per turn. Controls how many times execution can move between nodes in the agent network graph during a single conversation turn.</p></td><td><p>30</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>MODULE_GRAPH_ERROR_SETTINGS_MAX_REASONING_ITERATIONS</p></td><td><p>Maximum number of LLM reasoning loops allowed within a single node. Limits how many times the LLM can iterate on its reasoning before producing a result.</p></td><td><p>20</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>MODULE_GRAPH_ERROR_SETTINGS_MAX_SUBGRAPH_DEPTH</p></td><td><p>Maximum nesting depth for subgraphs. Controls how deeply agent networks can be nested within other agent networks.</p></td><td><p>10</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>MODULE_GRAPH_ERROR_SETTINGS_MAX_NODE_TOOL_CALL_ITERATIONS</p></td><td><p>Maximum number of tool executor runs allowed per node. Limits how many times a node can invoke tool execution during its processing.</p></td><td><p>20</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>MODULE_GRAPH_ERROR_SETTINGS_MAX_TURN_TOOL_CALL_COUNTS</p></td><td><p>Total number of tool invocations allowed across all nodes per turn. Provides a global limit on tool usage during a single conversation turn.</p></td><td><p>50</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>MODULE_GRAPH_ERROR_SETTINGS_MAX_STATE_SIZE_BYTES</p></td><td><p>Maximum accumulated state size in bytes. Limits the total amount of state data that can be accumulated during graph execution. Default is 10 MB (10485760 bytes).</p></td><td><p>10485760</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

Specify all runtime system limit variables as string values in the `exchange.json` file. All
variables are non-sensitive (`secret: false`).

# Building Agent Networks for Agent Fabric

> For the full documentation index, see: https://docs.mulesoft.com/llms.txt

An agent network is a coordinated group of agents, brokers, LLMs, and MCP servers that acts as a
central hub for defining, validating, and executing agentic processes across your enterprise.

An agent network provides the building blocks of your agentic deployment while MuleSoft Agent Fabric
helps you maximize the potential of every AI agent with centralized discovery, orchestration across
agents and tools, cross-ecosystem governance, and full transparency into agentic interactions.

You define your agent network in a simple, human-readable YAML file in Anypoint Code Builder. This
approach abstracts away the underlying technical complexities, allowing you to focus on the business
constraints and context of your process without needing to understand the inner workings of the
orchestration engine.

At the start of a new agent network project, MuleSoft provides a YAML template and Agent Script file
to give you a head start. You can use MuleSoft Vibes to configure your network, publish the assets
to Anypoint Exchange, and deploy your agent network instance.

## Key Benefits of Agent Networks

Create robust, automated agent networks with these key benefits.

- Simplified Development

  Define your agent processes in an intentional way using a simple YAML file, which is easier and
  faster than writing complex code.

- Safety and Governance

  Ensure control and compliance across every agent and tool interaction with enterprise-grade
  governance.

- Observability

  Gain insight into agent actions with a visual trace of their decision-making.

- Flexibility

  Coordinate any type of agent and tool, regardless of where it’s built and deployed so you can
  build a diverse network of agents.

- Tool and Agent Invocation

  Manage the invocation of both deterministic (tool-based) and probabilistic (LLM-based) actions.

## The Guided Determinism Pattern

Brokers in agent network 2.0 architecture use a guided deterministic approach by separating steps
requiring probabilistic LLM reasoning from those requiring deterministic control-flow logic.

- Probabilistic (LLM-based) nodes handle complex, open-ended decisions that require nuanced
  judgment, such as classification or AI-powered thinking.
- Deterministic nodes manage all remaining predefined execution paths, ensuring a fixed and
  guaranteed workflow after a key probabilistic judgment has been finalized.

This structure allows brokers to apply high-level LLM intelligence where complex judgment is needed,
while the overall agent graph maintains reliable, rule-based predictability across the operational
flow.

## Agent Network Components

Agent networks use LLMs for reasoning and planning capabilities and integrate with Anypoint
Connector for MCP (Model Context Protocol) and Anypoint Connector for Agent2Agent (A2A)
communication.

Broker

An intelligent routing service that coordinates task delegation across A2A-compliant agents in your
enterprise. You define a broker and its nodes in Agent Script. Nodes are connected in a graph that
encapsulates all steps that describe the orchestration of agents, tools, and LLMs. A graph-based
approach to agent brokers ensures that connected paths guarantee a specific order of operations and
enable more complex orchestration that combines deterministic and non-deterministic elements.

After you publish your agent network, brokers appear as specialized agents in Anypoint Exchange and
can be reused by other brokers.

A broker graph is composed of these elements:

Nodes

Each "step" within a graph. Nodes can be used to orchestrate actions with LLM-powered reasoning or
perform deterministic actions like routing.

Trigger

An entry point into a graph. Triggers specify events, calls, or messages that execute workflows. All
graphs must start on an A2A trigger.

Edges

Transitions from node to node. Input data enters the node and output data exits the node.

Agent

An autonomous software component that uses goals, context, and available tools, often via a LLM, to
decide and execute actions on behalf of a user or system.

Agents can be defined either locally in the agent network or externally in a different agent network
or elsewhere in your company. Your agent network can use both locally defined and externally defined
agents to complete tasks.

Agent assets must be A2A-compliant.

MCP server

A service that implements the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to expose tools and data to AI clients,
enabling LLMs to invoke external capabilities through a standard interface.

MCP servers can be defined either locally in the agent network or externally in a different agent
network or elsewhere in your company. Your agent network can use both locally defined and externally
defined MCP servers to complete tasks.

Registry

A section within an agent network project that defines the assets, connections, and policies
necessary to build, execute, and govern a broker. Assets defined in this section of an agent network
file are published to Exchange and become reusable. You can also reference existing assets from
Exchange in a graph without needing to define them in the registry section.

## Agent Network YAML and Agent Script

An agent network project defines a structured configuration for multi-agent systems, enabling
orchestration of AI agents with external services, tools, and inter-agent communication. This format
provides a declarative way to define agent capabilities, dependencies, and service integrations.

An agent network project includes these files:

/my-agent-network-project

- exchange.json
- agent-network.yaml /brokers
  - broker1.agent

* `exchange.json`: Contains asset metadata available in Anypoint Exchange after publishing your
  agent network assets.
* `agent-network.yaml`: Contains a registry section that defines Exchange assets used in your
  project and a context section that defines connections and policies for the project.
* `.agent` files: Contain broker and node definitions and configurations that enable multi-agent
  orchestration in your project.

For more information, see [Agent Network 2.0 Project File Reference](af-project-files).

> [!NOTE] For a complete, working example you can use as a starting point for your own agent network
> project, see [Example: Building an IT Investigation Broker](af-example-it-investigation-broker).
> The example walks through a fully configured `agent-network.yaml`, `exchange.json`, and `/brokers`
> directory that you can adapt to your own project.

## Agent Network Architecture

This diagram shows an agent network deployed to a shared space in CloudHub 2.0 using a single Omni
Gateway for ingress and egress. The network includes agents and MCP servers and is observed in
Anypoint Monitoring.

![an agent network deployed to a shared space in CloudHub 2 using a single mni Gateway for ingress and egress. The network includes agents and MCP servers and is observed in Anypoint Monitoring](_images/agent-fabric-architecture-v2-shared-space.png)

<table><tbody><tr><td><i data-value="1"></i><b>1</b></td><td>Publish the agentic assets to Anypoint Exchange for discovery and reuse after you define the agent network (brokers, agents, MCP servers) in the agent network YAML in Anypoint Code Builder.</td></tr><tr><td><i data-value="2"></i><b>2</b></td><td>Deploy the agentic assets to CloudHub 2.0 (managed in Runtime Manager).</td></tr><tr><td><i data-value="3"></i><b>3</b></td><td>Enforce policies, manage connections, and emit telemetry through a single Omni Gateway that handles both ingress to brokers/API endpoints and egress to external agents and services.<div><div data-type="NOTE">In a private space using a two-gateway configuration, policies, traffic, and data are handled by separate ingress and egress Omni Gateways.</div></div></td></tr><tr><td><i data-value="4"></i><b>4</b></td><td>Collect logs, metrics, and traces from Omni Gateway and runtimes in Anypoint Monitoring.</td></tr></tbody></table>

## Agent Network Assets in Anypoint Exchange

Agent network projects support these asset types in Exchange:

Agent Network

An agent network project is published in Exchange as an agent network asset. The asset is a .zip
file that contains all project files. To learn more, see
[Agent Network YAML and Agent Script](#yaml-and-agent-script) or
[Agent Network 2.0 Project File Reference](af-project-files).

Agents

Programs that perform tasks autonomously or semiautonomously. AI agents use the Agent2Agent (A2A)
protocol to communicate and collaborate with each other to perform tasks.

When you publish agent network projects to Exchange, the individual agentic assets defined in the
agent network project file are registered as either agents or MCP servers. Brokers are published
with the agent asset type and are automatically tagged as brokers for easy identification.

LLMs (Large Language Models)

AI assets for processing, understanding, and generating human-readable language. Agent network
projects support [various LLMs](#llm-support). The LLM asset type defines only the provider and
contract information. You define the model and connectivity details in the agent network file.

MCP Servers

Applications or APIs exposed through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). MCP is an open protocol
designed to standardize how applications provide context and capabilities to LLMs and AI agents. In
the agent network file, MCP server assets are defined as `Tools`.

## Large Language Models

Agent network brokers support the latest models from OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Bedrock OpenAI, and
Gemini, as well as LLM Proxies.

- [OpenAI](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models)
- [Azure OpenAI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/openai/concepts/models)
- [Bedrock OpenAI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/models-supported.html)

  > [!NOTE] Bedrock OpenAI uses the `openai.` prefix for model names (for example,
  > `openai.gpt-5.5`), which differs from the model names used with OpenAI and Azure OpenAI.

- [Gemini](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models)
- LLM Proxy

  Agent network brokers only support access to OpenAI and Gemini through
  [Omni Gateway LLM Proxy](../../gateway/latest/flex-gateway-llm-proxy). Transcoding other models to
  OpenAI format to use in agent networks is not supported.

This table details requirements and recommended models.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th><strong>Model Provider</strong></th><th><strong>Required Endpoint</strong></th><th><strong>Required Capabilities</strong></th><th><strong>Suggested Models</strong></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p>OpenAI</p></td><td><p><code>/responses</code></p></td><td><div><div><ul><li><p>Reasoning</p></li><li><p>Native structured output</p></li><li><p>Function and custom tool calling</p></li></ul></div></div></td><td><div><div><ul><li><p>For lower latency: GPT-5-mini</p></li><li><p>For complex reasoning: Evaluate models</p></li></ul></div></div></td></tr><tr><td><p>Gemini</p></td><td><p><code>/generateContent</code> (Native API)</p></td><td><div><div><ul><li><p>Native Thinking (via thinkingBudget and thinkingLevel)</p></li><li><p>Native structured output (responseSchema)</p></li><li><p>Function and custom tool calling</p></li></ul></div></div></td><td><div><div><ul><li><p>For lower latency: Gemini 2.5 Flash, Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite</p></li><li><p>For complex reasoning: Gemini 3 Pro (Deep Think capabilities)</p></li></ul></div></div></td></tr></tbody></table>

Agent networks support text-based messages and responses. Image and binary message types aren’t
supported.

For configuration options, see the [LLM Section](af-agent-script-reference#llm-section) of the Agent
Script file reference.

## A2A Protocol

The Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol governs agent-to-agent communication. This protocol powers
orchestration, observability, and governance features in agent networks. MuleSoft supports v1.0 of
the A2A Protocol Specification.

### Context and Task ID Scoping in Agent Networks

In MuleSoft agent networks, the brokers receiving a request always generate a `contextId` and
`taskId`. These IDs define the state and scope of a specific conversation between two agents. A
`taskId` is always matched to a `contextId`, but a `contextId` can exist without a `taskId`.

In a multi-agent network, a client sends a request to Broker_1 and Broker_1 generates the necessary
IDs for that request. When Broker_1 sends a new request to the next broker or non-broker agent in
line, that broker or non-broker agent establishes a unique `contextId` and `taskId` for the new
request.

> [!NOTE] Non-broker agents don’t have to generate a `contextId` and `taskId` when receiving
> requests from a client.

Consider a network with a client and two brokers (1 and 2).

- The IDs used between the client and Broker_1 are independent of the IDs used between Broker_1 and
  Broker_2.
- When Broker_1 delegates a task to Broker_2, Broker_2 (acting as a server) generates its own
  `contextId` and `taskId`.
- Broker_1 is responsible for maintaining a mapping between its own upstream `taskId` (used to
  respond to its client) and the downstream `taskId` it’s tracking with Broker_2.
- If Broker_2 requires more information (if it returns `status: input-required`), it provides a
  `contextId` and `taskId` to Broker_1. Broker_1 uses these IDs to provide the requested input to
  Broker_2. The client never sees Broker_2’s internal IDs.

<table><colgroup><col> <col> <col></colgroup><thead><tr><th>Relationship</th><th>Role</th><th>Logic</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><p>Client → Broker_1</p></td><td><p>Broker_1 is server</p></td><td><p>Generates <code>contextId_1</code> and <code>taskId_1</code> for the client.</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>Agent A → Broker_2</p></td><td><p>Broker_2 is server</p></td><td><p>Generates <code>contextId_2</code> and <code>taskId_2</code> for Broker_1.</p></td></tr><tr><td><p>Network broker</p></td><td><p>Broker_1</p></td><td><p>Broker_1 maps <code>contextId_1</code> and <code>taskId_1</code> to <code>contextId_2</code> and <code>taskId_2</code>.</p></td></tr></tbody></table>

For more information, see
[Life of a Task - Group Related Interactions](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/topics/life-of-a-task/).

> [!NOTE] With A2A v1.0, agent networks now support streaming with Server-Sent Events (SSE), both
> for calling A2A agents that support streaming and for streaming as an A2A endpoint itself.

- [Create Agent Networks](af-create-agent-network)
